title: Solid Cache Configuration
markdownDescription:
Configuration for [Solid Cache](https://github.com/rails/solid_cache), a database-backed ActiveSupport::Cache::Store. Solid Cache uses modern SSDs to provide a much larger cache than traditional memory-only stores like Redis or Memcached.

Configured by default in Rails 8+. See the [Solid Cache README](https://github.com/rails/solid_cache) for more information.

database.markdownDescription:
Name of a single database (from `config/database.yml`) to store the cache in. Shorthand for `connects_to: { database: { writing: <name> } }`.

Only one of `database`, `databases` or `connects_to` can be set. If none are set, Solid Cache uses the `ActiveRecord::Base` connection pool.

[Solid Cache Docs](https://github.com/rails/solid_cache#connection-configuration)

databases.markdownDescription:
Array of database shard names for multi-database cache setup. Uses Maglev consistent hashing to distribute cache entries.

Only one of `database`, `databases` or `connects_to` can be set.

Example: `[cache_shard1, cache_shard2, cache_shard3]`

[Solid Cache Docs](https://github.com/rails/solid_cache#sharding-the-cache)

connects_to.markdownDescription:
Passed directly to `SolidCache::Record.connects_to`. Use this for full control over the cache database connection (e.g. `database: { writing: :cache, reading: :cache_replica }` or `shards: { ... }`).

Only one of `database`, `databases` or `connects_to` can be set. `config.solid_cache.connects_to` overrides this value.

[Solid Cache Docs](https://github.com/rails/solid_cache#connection-configuration)

size_estimate_samples.markdownDescription:
Number of samples used to estimate the cache size when `max_size` is set.

Default: `10000`

encrypt.markdownDescription:
Enable encryption for cached values using Active Record Encryption. Requires setting up [Active Record Encryption](https://guides.rubyonrails.org/active_record_encryption.html).

Solid Cache uses optimized encryptor and serializer by default.

Default: `false`

store_options.markdownDescription: Cache store configuration options that control cache behavior, expiry, and size limits.

max_age.markdownDescription:
Maximum age of cache entries in seconds before they're eligible for deletion.

Default: `2.weeks` (1,209,600 seconds)

Can be set to `nil` but not recommended unless using `max_entries` to limit cache size.

max_size.markdownDescription:
Maximum total size of cache entries in bytes. When exceeded, Solid Cache will delete old entries.

Default: `nil` (no limit)

Size is estimated by sampling entries, so this is approximate.

max_entries.markdownDescription:
Maximum number of entries allowed in the cache. When exceeded, Solid Cache will delete old entries.

Default: `nil` (no limit)

The number of entries is estimated from the difference between the maximum and minimum entry IDs.

expiry_batch_size.markdownDescription:
Batch size used when deleting old records. Expiry is triggered once the write counter reaches 50% of this value.

Default: `100`

[Solid Cache Docs](https://github.com/rails/solid_cache#cache-expiry)

expiry_method.markdownDescription:
How cache expiry is run: on a background thread, or by enqueuing a `SolidCache::ExpiryJob`.

Must be a Ruby symbol (e.g. `:job`) — plain strings are rejected.

Default: `:thread`

expiry_queue.markdownDescription:
Queue that expiry jobs are added to when `expiry_method` is `:job`.

Default: `default`

shards.markdownDescription: The database shards (from the configured `connects_to`/`databases`) that this cache store uses.

cluster.markdownDescription: Options for the cache database cluster, e.g. `{ shards: [database1, database2] }`.

clusters.markdownDescription: An array of cluster option hashes. Multiple clusters are no longer supported.

active_record_instrumentation.markdownDescription:
Whether to instrument the cache's Active Record queries.

Default: `true`

clear_with.markdownDescription:
How `Rails.cache.clear` deletes entries: by truncating the table or with `DELETE`.

Default: `truncate`, except in the test environment where it is `delete` (truncating breaks transactional tests in MySQL).

max_key_bytesize.markdownDescription:
Maximum size of a normalized key in bytes. Lower this if your database can't create the 1024-byte key index.

Default: `1024`

[Solid Cache Docs](https://github.com/rails/solid_cache#index-size-limits)

expires_in.markdownDescription: Default relative expiration time for cache entries, in seconds (standard `ActiveSupport::Cache::Store` option).

race_condition_ttl.markdownDescription: Default number of seconds during which an expired value can be reused while a new value is being regenerated (standard `ActiveSupport::Cache::Store` option).

compress.markdownDescription:
Whether to compress cache entries larger than `compress_threshold` (standard `ActiveSupport::Cache::Store` option).

Default: `true`

compress_threshold.markdownDescription:
Size in bytes above which cache entries are compressed (standard `ActiveSupport::Cache::Store` option).

Default: `1024` (`1.kilobyte`)

serializer.markdownDescription: Preconfigured serializer for cached values, as a Ruby symbol (standard `ActiveSupport::Cache::Store` option). Defaults to the serializer for `config.active_support.cache_format_version`. `:message_pack` requires the `msgpack` gem.

skip_nil.markdownDescription:
Prevent caching `nil` results from `fetch` (standard `ActiveSupport::Cache::Store` option).

Default: `false`

namespace.markdownDescription:
Namespace prefix for all cache keys. Useful for sharing a cache database across multiple applications or environments.

Example: `myapp_production` results in keys like `myapp_production:users/1`
